text:
samantha: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC re: dashboard refresh gating. TL;DR: we need a lightweight fallback when RBAC evaluation lags so dashboards don't time out for users. Proposal: maintain a per-tenant visibility bitmap (or similar compact structure) that query layer can consult to short-circuit full auth fanout. Thoughts?

matt: I like the short-circuit idea. Main concern is invalidation complexity and memory growth if we store full bitsets per tenant. Also rollout strategy?

deepa: What about Bloom filters instead of exact bitsets? Much smaller. We accept some false positives but final row-level auth check can still run for positives. False negatives would be bad though so we need parameters tuned.

samantha: Good point. Bloom reduces RAM but increases extra auth checks. We need to balance extra backends calls vs memory. For the common case (tenant-level visibility mostly stable) false positive rate could be 1-2% and that's probably ok.

leo: We already have a projection-level tenant-visibility cache in the projection service (used for tile materialization). Could we repurpose that rather than adding a new datastore? Might save effort but projection ownership and release timelines are a concern.

matt: Reuse sounds ideal but signal fidelity differs. Projection cache keys are per-entity; we need a compact thing keyed by dashboard-id -> visible-tenants. Also need cross-region replication if we want low-latency reads in EU/US.

samantha: Agreed. For rollout I propose: 1) implement a Bloom-backed visibility cache in query-side edge, 2) wire telemetry and runtime flags, 3) canary to 5% tenants, observe authz_fallback_rate and stale_dashboard_served metrics, 4) if stable, migrate projection cache consumers to the same API.

infra-bot: deploy:plan posted. Suggested canary window 48h and outage rollback if stale_dashboard_served > 0.5% or authz_error_increase > 0.2%. See https://confluence/internal/infra/canary-guidance

matt: SLO question: If authz evaluation > 200ms for a request, do we prefer to serve a slightly stale snapshot or fail the request? For product safety I'd rather serve a stale snapshot with an indicator in the UI.

deepa: That aligns with my thinking. Add a per-response header/field like `x-dashboard-stale-reason` and `stale_from_ts` so UI can show a warning and allow manual refresh.

samantha: Also propose a small backoff/refresh loop: when stale snapshot served, spawn low-priority background revalidate to update visibility cache. Keep TTLs conservative so we don't thrash the auth service.

leo: We should enumerate telemetry counters before dev. Minimum: `visibility_cache_hit`, `visibility_cache_miss`, `stale_dashboard_served`, `authz_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99`, `visibility_invalidation_count`. Add a label for rollout cohort.

matt: Runbook: If `stale_dashboard_served` spikes > threshold, first step is to disable bloom fallback (feature flag), then investigate `authz_latency` spikes and authz service errors. Escalate to infra if cross-region replication lag is implicated.

samantha: For policy, fallback behavior should be DENY-by-default for rows where we can't confirm visibility to avoid data leakage. Bloom false positives lead to extra checks, but false negatives (if they happen) are not tolerable. We'll tune parameters to avoid negatives.

deepa: Sounds good. One more thought: make the cache opt-in per-dashboard via metadata so we can pilot only non-sensitive dashboards first.

samantha: Good call. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with the experiment plan, rollout knobs, metrics, and a sample feature-flag config. Example flag snippet:```json
{"feature": "visibility_bloom_fallback", "cohort": "canary", "max_false_positive_rate": "0.02", "canary_tenants": ["tenant-123","tenant-456"]}
```

infra-bot: ack. I'll create the canary rollout ticket and add the monitoring alerts.

samantha: Thanks all — will ping the thread when RFC is ready for review. :thumbsup:
